title: X-ray analysis found a molecular tilt gradient at a buried transistor interface
summary: An optical model built with hierarchical clustering helped researchers infer a distinct molecular state at the buried interface of a zinc phthalocyanine film on silica. Fitting resonant soft X-ray reflectivity gave a molecular tilt of about 38° at the interface and 69.6° in the bulk, with an interface transition length of about 1.49 nanometers. The inference depends on the optical and structural models. A second film supported the density gradient, while its measurement could not independently resolve orientation. The results are from the October 29 revision of an October 22 arXiv preprint.
ai_technology: Hierarchical agglomerative clustering; ML-DFT optical model
organization: Washington State University; Australian Synchrotron, ANSTO; Prince Sattam bin Abdulaziz University

source_review.scope: Latest arXiv v2 PDF front matter, main reflectivity fit and interfacial structure results, clustering methods and supplementary comparison, plus version metadata

evidence.tested: The researchers collected energy- and polarization-dependent soft X-ray reflectivity, compared discrete-layer and gradient fits and assessed sensitivity. Diffraction informed the structural interpretation; independent-film nonresonant reflectivity checked density.
evidence.unknown: The angle and gradient depend on the fitted model. The second film did not independently establish orientation, and alternative microscopic packing mechanisms were not fully resolved.
evidence.ai_role: Hierarchical clustering converted calculated electronic transition dipoles into a compact optical representation, refined against independent absorption measurements, for the depth-dependent reflectivity model.
